text: HDFC Bank's 3.3% five-year CAGR and 15% off its highs show the merger overhang is still weighing, but the 11.8% ten-year CAGR and 41 analyst buys versus zero sells tell you the franchise compounding hasn't broken. Net income held above Rs 1.5 lakh crore in the last two quarters while the stock drifted, so forward earnings yield is quietly improving. For the client's car/battery theme, the only Indian names fitting Rs 10k are Exide (37 shares at Rs 272) and Amara Raja (9 shares at Rs 1,100), but both run sub-8% operating margins — too thin to fund a lithium pivot without dilution. On the US side, fractional Tesla at $300+ fits the $100 budget, yet a 2.0 beta and 70% max drawdown make it a lottery ticket, not a compounder. IPOs with $10 or Rs 10k remain structurally impossible: US minimums start at $500, Indian SME lots at Rs 1 lakh, and any listing pop faces 20% STCG plus Rs 38 round-trip on Zerodha delivery.
